1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: jq-based overlay for ~/.claude/keybindings.json.
3	#
4	# This file pairs with dot_claude/modify_settings.json (same shape, same jq
5	# tooling). The keybindings file is conservatively managed: we deliberately
6	# do NOT ship the full default keymap, because Claude Code can introduce new
7	# bindings or rename existing actions in any release, and a fully managed
8	# copy would silently diverge.
9	#
10	# What this overlay enforces today:
11	#   - The two metadata fields ($schema, $docs) at the top of the file. They
12	#     give editors / agents the right schema URL for autocomplete and the
13	#     right docs URL for action-name lookups. See:
14	#       Schema: https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-keybindings.json
15	#       Docs:   https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings
16	#
17	# What this overlay deliberately does NOT enforce yet:
18	#   - Any entries inside `.bindings` (the array of {context, bindings}
19	#     objects). A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` merge replaces arrays wholesale,
20	#     so dropping bindings overrides into this overlay's `.bindings` would
21	#     clobber every default Claude Code ships. If you want to add personal
22	#     binding overrides, extend the jq filter below to merge by `.context`
23	#     (similar to how dot_claude/modify_settings.json appends hook entries
24	#     by .hooks[0].command). Until that happens, treat the live file as the
25	#     source of truth for actual bindings and only edit it in-place.
26	#
27	# Why `modify_` and not `create_`:
28	#   - `create_` would seed once and then never enforce $schema/$docs; new
29	#     machines could drift if the upstream URLs change.
30	#   - `modify_` runs on every `chezmoi apply`, so the metadata stays
31	#     synchronised with what we've checked in here.
32	#
33	# Bootstrap (fresh machine, no live file yet):
34	#   - chezmoi pipes empty stdin into the script. We emit a minimal stub
35	#     that contains only the metadata fields — no bindings. Claude Code on
36	#     first launch falls back to its built-in defaults for any binding the
37	#     file doesn't define, then may write the file back with concrete
38	#     entries; a subsequent apply will merge $schema/$docs in.
39	#
40	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
41	#
42	# See: docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md (user-facing rationale, action
43	# namespaces, the chat:cycleMode-only mode-jump limitation).
44	set -eu
45	
46	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
47	{
48	  "$schema": "https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-keybindings.json",
49	  "$docs": "https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings"
50	}
51	JSON
52	)
53	
54	base=$(cat)
55	
56	# Bootstrap path: live file does not exist yet. Emit just the overlay so
57	# the file is well-formed when Claude Code reads it on its next launch.
58	if [ -z "$base" ]; then
59	  printf '%s\n' "$overlay"
60	  exit 0
61	fi
62	
63	# Steady-state path: deep-merge our metadata onto the live file. The live
64	# .bindings array is preserved verbatim — `. * $overlay` replaces arrays
65	# wholesale only at matching key paths, and our overlay has no .bindings
66	# key, so the live array is left untouched.
67	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '. * $overlay'
68

7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces
9	# arrays wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would
10	# silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and
11	# CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
12	#
13	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
14	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
15	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
16	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
17	# notify.sh while CodeIsland (or any other tool) freely manages its own
18	# parallel entries in the same event arrays.
19	#
20	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
21	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.

54	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
55	  },
56	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {

59	        "source": "github",
60	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
61	      }
62	    }
63	  },

3	#

7	# paths with absolute machine-local prefixes. We enforce only stable user
8	# preferences and let everything else through verbatim.
9	#

11	# the new contents on stdout. `jq '. * $overlay'` does recursive object merge.
12	#

19	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).

23	{{ template "agents/opencode.overlay.json" . }}
24	JSON
25	)
26	
27	base=$(cat)
28	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script body: deep-merge a shared overlay into an editor's settings.json.
3	#
4	# Shared across VSCode (Code), Cursor, and Antigravity on both macOS
5	# (~/Library/Application Support/<Editor>/User/settings.json) and Linux
6	# (~/.config/<Editor>/User/settings.json). Each editor's modify_settings.json.tmpl
7	# is a 1-liner that includes this template.
8	#
9	# Why overlay (not whole-file): the live settings.json in each editor is a
10	# museum of project- and machine-specific junk (remote hosts, extension keys,
11	# one-off editor UI nudges). Tracking the whole file produces constant diff.
12	# `jq '. * $overlay'` enforces ONLY the keys declared in $overlay; everything
13	# else stays verbatim.
14	#
15	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json.
16	# Per-editor deltas (future): add a sibling editor/overlay.<editor>.json and
17	# a second `jq '. * $extra'` pass; wire it in below. Minimal scope ships the
18	# shared overlay only.
19	#
20	# JSONC handling: VSCode / Cursor / Antigravity all write settings.json as
21	# JSONC (JSON with `//` and `/* */` comments plus trailing commas), but `jq`
22	# only reads strict JSON. The inline Python preprocessor below strips those
23	# while respecting string literals (so URLs like `https://...` inside strings
24	# are preserved). Normalisation means the managed settings.json will NOT
25	# preserve user-authored comments -- if you value them, keep notes in a
26	# sidecar file.
27	#
28	# Failure mode: if the live file is malformed beyond JSONC (e.g. unbalanced
29	# braces), jq exits non-zero and chezmoi skips this file for the apply. The
30	# broken live file is left untouched.
31	#
32	# Requires: jq + python3 (both installed by the `base` ansible role; system
33	# python3 is also pre-installed on macOS). On a fresh-box first apply
34	# neither is guaranteed yet (ansible runs AFTER the file-apply phase), so
35	# this script falls back to passing the live file through unchanged when
36	# either dependency is missing — the next apply does the real merge. See
37	# pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
38	set -eu
39	
40	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
41	{{ template "editor/overlay.json" . }}
42	JSON
43	)
44	
45	base=$(cat)
46	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'
47	
48	# Cold-start fallback: pick a python (system python3 first, else uv-managed
49	# python ≥3.11 which bootstrap installs). The JSONC stripper needs only
50	# `sys` + `re` from stdlib — any python3 works. `set --` (positional args)
51	# is used so the multi-arg `uv run …` form survives `set -u` + word-split.
52	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -c
54	elif command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
55	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --python '>=3.11' python -c
56	else
57	  printf '%s\n' "editor/modify.sh: neither python3 nor uv found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after ansible bootstrap." >&2
58	  printf '%s' "$base"
59	  exit 0
60	fi
61	
62	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
63	  printf '%s\n' "editor/modify.sh: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
64	  printf '%s' "$base"
65	  exit 0
66	fi
67	
68	printf '%s' "$base" | "$@" 'import sys, re
69	data = sys.stdin.read()
70	if not data.strip():
71	    data = "{}"
72	out = []
73	i, n = 0, len(data)
74	in_str = False
75	esc = False
76	quote = None
77	while i < n:
78	    c = data[i]
79	    if in_str:
80	        out.append(c)
81	        if esc:
82	            esc = False
83	        elif c == "\\":
84	            esc = True
85	        elif c == quote:
86	            in_str = False
87	        i += 1
88	        continue
89	    if c == "\"" or c == "\x27":
90	        in_str = True
91	        quote = c
92	        out.append(c)
93	        i += 1
94	        continue
95	    if c == "/" and i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == "/":
96	        while i < n and data[i] != "\n":
97	            i += 1
98	        continue
99	    if c == "/" and i + 1 < n and data[i + 1] == "*":
100	        i += 2
101	        while i + 1 < n and not (data[i] == "*" and data[i + 1] == "/"):
102	            i += 1
103	        i += 2
104	        continue
105	    out.append(c)
106	    i += 1
107	stripped = "".join(out)
108	stripped = re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", stripped)
109	sys.stdout.write(stripped)
110	' | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '. * $overlay'
111

#!/bin/sh
# Simulate cold-start: hide jq + python3 from PATH and run each modify_ script.
# Expect: stdout == stdin, stderr contains "passing live file through", exit 0.

set -eu
DOTFILES="/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi"
ISOLATED_PATH="/usr/bin:/bin"  # no jq, no python3, no uv on a stock system

# Files that need the env-var template substitution stripped (the .tmpl ones).
# We test the source file body directly; chezmoi template substitution only
# matters for the overlay literals which don't affect the cold-start branch.

run_test() {
  local name="$1" file="$2" input="$3"
  printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$name"
  out=$(PATH="$ISOLATED_PATH" sh -c "printf '%s' '$input' | sh '$file'" 2>err.log) || rc=$?
  rc="${rc:-0}"
  printf 'rc=%s\n' "$rc"
  printf 'stdout=%s\n' "$out"
  printf 'stderr='
  cat err.log
  if [ "$rc" = "0" ] && [ "$out" = "$input" ] && grep -q "passing live file through" err.log; then
    printf 'PASS\n'
  else
    printf 'FAIL\n'
    return 1
  fi
}

# Note: .tmpl files contain chezmoi template syntax. We can't run them directly.
# Instead, render via chezmoi execute-template first.
render_and_test() {
  local name="$1" tmpl="$2" input="$3"
  rendered=$(mktemp)
  ( cd "$DOTFILES" && chezmoi execute-template < "$tmpl" > "$rendered" )
  run_test "$name" "$rendered" "$input"
  rm -f "$rendered"
}

# 1. Plain (non-template) modify_ files
run_test "modify_keybindings.json" "$DOTFILES/dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json" '{"existing":"value"}'
run_test "modify_settings.json (claude)" "$DOTFILES/dot_claude/modify_settings.json" '{"already":"there"}'

# 2. .tmpl files (need chezmoi to render template syntax first)
render_and_test "modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" "$DOTFILES/dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" '{"version":3,"skills":{"foo":{"source":"x"}}}'
render_and_test "modify_opencode.json.tmpl" "$DOTFILES/dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl" '{"runtime":"keep"}'
render_and_test "modify_tui.json.tmpl" "$DOTFILES/dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl" '{"theme":"dark"}'
render_and_test "modify_cli-config.json.tmpl" "$DOTFILES/dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl" '{"authInfo":"secret"}'

printf '\n=== ALL PASS ===\n'
OUTER
chmod +x /tmp/test_pass_through.sh && /tmp/test_pass_through.sh

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
53	
54	## File template
55	
56	See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
57	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
58	or copy the structure of an existing entry below.
59

```

# `modify_*` scripts crash with `jq: command not found` on a fresh-box first apply

**Symptoms** (grep this section): `jq: command not found`; `chezmoi: .agents/.skill-lock.json: exit status 127`; `chezmoi: .claude/settings.json: exit status 127`; `chezmoi: .config/opencode/opencode.json: exit status 127`; `chezmoi: .cursor/cli-config.json: exit status 127`; `/tmp/<random>..skill-lock.json: line NN: jq: command not found`; `chezmoi update --init` aborts immediately after `[SUCCESS] Bootstrap complete!`
**First seen**: 2026-05 (yzhang@idc-server104, `centos_server` profile, `noRoot=true` — first cold-start after the profile was added in commit `e8de50d`)
**Affects**: every fresh machine where `jq` is not pre-installed (CentOS 7 noRoot, minimal Ubuntu Server, fresh Linux containers, older macOS without `/usr/bin/jq`); macOS Sequoia 15+ ships `/usr/bin/jq` system-side and is *not* affected
**Status**: fixed — every `modify_*` script now `command -v` guards `jq` (and `python3` for editor overlays) and falls back to pass-through

## Symptom

On `chezmoi update --init` (or `chezmoi apply`) on a fresh box:

\```
[yzhang@idc-server104 chezmoi]$ chezmoi update --init
Already up to date.
[INFO] useChineseMirror=true: using Aliyun (Homebrew) + TUNA (Rustup / mise) mirrors
[INFO] noRoot mode: Skipping Linuxbrew installation (requires sudo)
[INFO] uv is already installed
[INFO] Installing mise...
…
[INFO] ansible is already installed
[INFO] Installing ansible-galaxy collections...
…
[SUCCESS] Bootstrap complete!
/tmp/934409313..skill-lock.json: line 59: jq: command not found
chezmoi: .agents/.skill-lock.json: exit status 127
\```

`chezmoi apply` halts with exit 127. Subsequent run-scripts (the ansible
roles in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`) never execute, so
`jq` never gets installed, so the next `chezmoi apply` fails the same way.
The user is stuck in a bootstrap cycle that requires manual intervention to
break.

## Root cause

`chezmoi apply` runs in three phases, in order:

1. `run_once_before_*` scripts → `00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` installs **uv, mise, ansible-core, Linuxbrew (rooted Linux only), Homebrew (macOS)**. Bootstrap **does not install `jq`** (or `ripgrep`, `fd`, `python3` — those come from ansible).
2. **File-application phase** — chezmoi processes every `modify_*` script. `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl:58` (and several others) hard-call `jq` with `set -eu` and no `command -v` guard.
3. `run_onchange_after_*` scripts → `20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` runs the `base` ansible role, which installs `jq` (apt/yum/brew system path + a noRoot user-level GitHub-release fallback at `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:248-275`).

On a fresh box, phase 2 needs `jq` but `jq` is only installed in phase 3 →
chicken-and-egg. The `set -eu` in the modify_ script + chezmoi's behaviour
of treating any non-zero exit from a modify_ script as a fatal apply error
means chezmoi aborts before phase 3 runs.

This was previously masked on personal Macs (Homebrew installs `jq` long
before the dotfiles run) and on Ubuntu desktop (jq usually comes pre-loaded
or via a base apt package the user already installed). It surfaced on
CentOS 7 noRoot — see [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](centos7-noroot.md),
which lists `jq` as one of the binaries missing on that profile but didn't
yet connect it to a bootstrap-order failure.

### Audit — `modify_*` scripts and their dependencies

| File | Calls | Cold-start safe? |
|---|---|---|
| `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ guard added |
| `.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh` (covers VSCode + Cursor + Antigravity × Linux + macOS = 6 wrappers) | `python3` + `jq` | ✅ both guarded; uv→python3 fallback chain |
| `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl` | `uv`/`python3` | ✅ already had guards (`:47-55`) |
| `dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ already had guard (`:28-31`) |
| `dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl` | `jq` | ✅ already had guard (`:19-21`) |

## Workaround

If you're hit by an unfixed version of this repo (i.e. before the guard
commits landed), break the cycle by manually installing `jq` user-level —
same source the `base` ansible role uses (`base/tasks/main.yml:248-275`):

\```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/;s/armv7l/armhf/')
curl -fsSL -o ~/.local/bin/jq \
  "https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/latest/download/jq-linux-${ARCH}"
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/jq
hash -r
chezmoi apply
\```

After ansible's `base` role runs (during the next `chezmoi apply`), it will
overwrite `~/.local/bin/jq` with the same binary — idempotent.

On macOS pre-Sequoia, the equivalent is `brew install jq` (or download the
`jq-macos-arm64` / `jq-macos-amd64` binary from the same GitHub releases
page).

## Prevention

The guard pattern adopted in this repo, lifted from
[`run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl:32-35`](../.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl):

\```sh
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s\n' "modify_<file>: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
  printf '%s' "$base"
  exit 0
fi
\```

The `printf '%s' "$base"` is the load-bearing line — chezmoi sees stdout
matching the live file → no-op for that target → apply continues.

For `editor/modify.sh` (which needs both `python3` and `jq`), the python3
side gets a uv→system-python3 fallback chain mirroring
[`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl:47-55`](../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl).
`uv` is bootstrap-guaranteed, so the chain almost always succeeds; if
neither is available, both pass through.

The contract for future `modify_*` scripts is documented in
[`docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md) →
"Bootstrap-order contract".

## Related

- [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](centos7-noroot.md) — sibling pitfall: lists `jq` (and others) as missing on noRoot CentOS but doesn't enumerate the bootstrap-cycle failure mode this doc covers
- [`docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md) → "Bootstrap-order contract" — design contract for `modify_*` scripts (must tolerate post-bootstrap-installed tools)
- [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](../docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) — separate concern: install vs upgrade split, why `chezmoi apply` is install-only
- [`dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:248-275`](../dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml) — the canonical user-level (noRoot) `jq` install path: download from GitHub releases into `~/.local/bin/jq`

```text
62	
63	  ```bash
64	  cp ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json)"
65	  ```
66	
67	- **Typical use**: LazyVim `lazy-lock.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_confignvimcreate_lazy-lockjson--seed-once-never-overwrite)), SSH `config` skeleton, first-run app baselines.
68	
69	### `modify_` — content is a script, not a file
70	
71	- **Effect**: The source file is an executable **script**. chezmoi pipes the current target contents into stdin; the script writes the new target contents to stdout. Lets you manage part of a file (e.g. via `jq`, `sed`, `awk`) while leaving the rest alone.
72	- **`chezmoi add`**: do **not** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite your script with the live file contents.
73	- **Alternative form**: put `chezmoi:modify-template` in the script body to switch it into template mode (the current contents arrive as `.chezmoi.stdin`). See [Manage part, but not all, of a file](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/manage-different-types-of-file/#manage-part-but-not-all-of-a-file).
74	- **Typical use**: Claude Code `settings.json` (see the [case study below](#dot_claudemodify_settingsjson--partial-json-management-via-jq)), Docker `config.json` proxies, INI files with a mix of managed and runtime-written keys.
75	
76	### `exact_` — directory is canonical (prune extras)
77	
78	- **Effect**: On apply, chezmoi **removes** any file inside the target directory that is not present in source. Directory-only prefix.
79	- **`chezmoi add`**: safe for individual files inside the directory, but be aware of the semantic trap — next apply will clean up anything that drifted in.
80	- **Risk**: Very easy to accidentally delete machine-local artifacts (caches, plugin installs) that happen to live inside the directory.
81	- **Typical use**: directories you truly own end-to-end and that are small / stable. Avoid for any directory that mixes managed config with runtime state.
82	
83	### `literal_` — stop parsing attributes
84	
85	- **Effect**: Tells chezmoi to stop interpreting the rest of the filename as attributes. Used when an actual filename starts with something like `create` or `run` and you want chezmoi to treat it literally.
86	- **`chezmoi add`**: green-light, but remember the prefix exists for a filename-level reason — blindly renaming it later can break the mapping.
87	- **Typical use**: uncommon. Corner cases like a literal `run_` or `dot_` in a filename.
88	
89	### `remove_` — assert removal
90	
91	- **Effect**: Declares that the target should be **absent**. On apply, chezmoi removes the file/symlink (or empty directory) if it exists. The source file's body is not a content source — it is a presence assertion.
92	- **`chezmoi add`**: does not apply (there is no live content to sync back).
93	- **Typical use**: cleaning up stale configs after migrating tools. Often combined with a template so it only fires on specific hosts.
94	
95	### `encrypted_` — encrypt at rest
96
```

#!/bin/sh

  name="$1"; tmpl_or_script="$2"; input="$3"; expected_substring="$4"
  printf '\n=== HAPPY: %s ===\n' "$name"
  if [ "${tmpl_or_script##*.}" = "tmpl" ] || echo "$tmpl_or_script" | grep -q "tmpl$"; then
    rendered=$(mktemp)
    ( cd "$DOTFILES" && chezmoi execute-template < "$tmpl_or_script" > "$rendered" )

    rm -f "$rendered"

  printf 'output:\n%s\n' "$out"
  if echo "$out" | grep -q "$expected_substring"; then

All seven scripts now: missing tool → write live file unchanged to stdout + warn to stderr + exit 0. Idempotent — next apply (after ansible installs the missing tool) does the real merge.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
modify_: pass-through when jq/python3 missing (cold-start fix)

`chezmoi apply` runs modify_* scripts during the file-application phase,
BEFORE `run_onchange_after_*` (where ansible installs jq, python3,
ripgrep, fd, …). Bootstrap only guarantees uv/mise/ansible-core. On a
fresh box without jq pre-installed (CentOS 7 noRoot, minimal Ubuntu
Server, fresh Linux containers, pre-Sequoia macOS), a bare `set -eu`
modify_ script that hard-calls jq aborts the whole apply with exit 127
— and ansible never reaches the role that would have installed jq, so
subsequent applies fail the same way (chicken-and-egg).

Add `command -v` guards to all 7 modify_ scripts that needed them; on
missing tool, write the live file to stdout unchanged, warn to stderr,
exit 0. Mirrors the existing pattern in
.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl:32-35.

Files (jq guards):
- dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
- dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json
- dot_claude/modify_settings.json
- dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl
- dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl
- dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl

.chezmoitemplates/editor/modify.sh (covers VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity ×
Linux+macOS = 6 wrappers): adds both a jq guard and a uv→python3
fallback chain; uses `set --` + `"$@"` so the multi-arg `uv run` form
survives `set -u` and word-splitting.

Already-safe (had guards): dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl,
dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl, dot_docker/modify_config.json.tmpl.

Docs:
- pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md (new) — symptom-titled
  trap doc with verbatim error message, audit table, and manual
  curl-jq-into-~/.local/bin workaround
- docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md — new "Bootstrap-order contract"
  subsection codifying the rule for future modify_ scripts

Reported by yzhang@idc-server104 (centos_server profile, noRoot=true).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git status --short

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Look up documented workaround for this exact loop

`grep -A 30 "## Workaround\|## Resolution\|## Fix" pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md 2>/dev/null | head -60`

```text
## Fix (the atomic pipeline)

Do the redaction without ever printing the matched bytes, then stage and
commit in **one** bash command so SpecStory has no window to write a new
copy:

```bash
FILE=.specstory/history/<active-session>.md

# 1. Redact in place. NEVER use grep/awk/sed in a way that prints the match.
python3 -c "
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('$FILE')
s = p.read_text()
s2 = re.sub(r'ey[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}',
            '<REDACTED-JWT>', s)
p.write_text(s2)
"

# 2. Stage the redacted snapshot. From this moment, the index is frozen —
# any later specstory write only affects the worktree, not the commit.
git add "$FILE"

# 3. Commit. Pre-commit will stash any post-stage worktree drift, run on
# the staged (redacted) version, find nothing, and commit cleanly.
git commit -m "..."
```

The redaction regex above (`ey[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.{10,}\.{10,}`) is
JWT-shaped (3 base64url segments separated by dots) and catches the common
case. Adjust per the actual leak class.
```
</details></tool-use>

commit bdaf720ac951cac426fe041d002b8962a40314e9
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed May 6 22:44:51 2026 +0800

    skill-lock: replace jq IN/1 with as-bound index/1 (jq 1.4+ compatible)
    
    CentOS 7's EPEL jq is 1.5; `IN/1` was added in jq 1.6. The merger
    script aborted with `jq: error: IN/1 is not defined at <top-level>`
    during `chezmoi apply` on CentOS 7, surfaced by
    `just docker-build-centos7-noroot`. Rewrote the predicate as
    `select(.key as $k | [...] | index($k))` which works on every
    chezmoi-supported jq (1.4+). Verified semantically equivalent against
    the existing Ubuntu jq 1.7 with a contrived merge case (live key
    preserves installedAt, managed values overwrite source/sourceUrl,
    non-allowlisted keys from managed are stripped).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
3	# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
4	#
5	# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
6	# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
7	# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
8	# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
9	# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
10	# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
11	#
12	# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
13	# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
14	# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
15	# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
16	# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
17	#
18	# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
19	# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
20	# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
21	#
22	<<<<<<< HEAD
23	# Requires: jq 1.4+ (1.4+ for `index/1`, NOT 1.6+ — keep this script
24	# compatible with CentOS 7's EPEL jq 1.5 since `IN/1` was added in 1.6).
25	=======
26	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
27	# apply jq is not yet installed, so this script falls back to passing the
28	# live file through unchanged — the next apply (after ansible) does the real
29	# merge. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
30	>>>>>>> 4c58013 (modify_: pass-through when jq/python3 missing (cold-start fix))
31	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
32	set -eu
33	
34	managed=$(cat <<'JSON'
35	{
36	  "version": 3,
37	  "skills": {
38	    "project-knowledge-harness": {
39	      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
40	      "sourceType": "github",
41	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git",
42	      "skillPath": "skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md"
43	    },
44	    "find-skills": {
45	      "source": "vercel-labs/skills",
46	      "sourceType": "github",
47	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills.git",
48	      "skillPath": "skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	JSON
53	)
54	
55	base=$(cat)
56	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'
57	
58	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which
59	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase. On the first `chezmoi apply` of a fresh
60	# box, pass the live (or empty-seeded) file through unchanged and warn — the
61	# next apply (after ansible installs jq) will perform the real merge. See
62	# pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md for the audit + rationale.
63	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	  printf '%s\n' "modify_dot_skill-lock.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
65	  printf '%s' "$base"
66	  exit 0
67	fi
68	
69	# Merge strategy:
70	#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
71	#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
72	#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
73	#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
74	#     (those are the contract we enforce).
75	#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
76	#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
77	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
78	  . as $base
79	  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
80	  | ($managed.skills // {}) as $managed_skills
81	  | {
82	      version: ([($base.version // 0), ($managed.version // 0)] | max),
83	      skills: (
84	        $live_skills
85	        + (
86	            $managed_skills
87	            | to_entries
88	            | map({
89	                key: .key,
90	                value: (
91	                  ($live_skills[.key] // {})
92	                  + (.value | with_entries(select(.key as $k | ["source","sourceType","sourceUrl","skillPath"] | index($k))))
93	                )
94	              })
95	            | from_entries
96	          )
97	      )
98	    }
99	    + (if ($base.dismissed // null) != null         then {dismissed:         $base.dismissed}         else {} end)
100	    + (if ($base.lastSelectedAgents // null) != null then {lastSelectedAgents: $base.lastSelectedAgents} else {} end)
101	'
102

Date:   Wed May 6 22:27:17 2026 +0800

    docker: install jq + force UTF-8 locale on CentOS 7
    
    Fixes two bugs surfaced by exercising centos7 / rocky9 builds:
    
    1. jq missing during `chezmoi apply` — the modify_ scripts under
       dot_agents/ (and others) shell out to jq during chezmoi's apply
       phase, which runs BEFORE the ansible base role can install jq
       system-wide. Result: `.agents/.skill-lock.json: exit status 127`
       (jq: command not found). Verified: ubuntu:24.04, rockylinux:9 and
       centos:7 all ship without jq, so this is a latent bug in the
       existing Ubuntu Dockerfile too — `just docker-test` would have
       regressed since commit 9eb1fc2 added the modify_ skill-lock script.
       Fix: add jq to the package-install step in all three Dockerfiles
       (apt for ubuntu, yum+epel for centos7, dnf for rocky9).
    
    2. CentOS 7 base image leaves LANG unset → ansible-galaxy fails with
       "Ansible requires the locale encoding to be UTF-8; Detected None."
       The bootstrap's locale-fix branch only triggers on `cannot set`
       errors from `locale`, which a clean centos:7 doesn't emit (LANG is
       simply absent). Fix: install glibc-common and pin LANG/LC_ALL=
       en_US.UTF-8 via ENV in Dockerfile.centos7 so chezmoi/ansible inherit
       a working locale unconditionally.
    
    Also tracks the prior `--promptString "profile (...)"` mismatch as
    pitfalls/chezmoi-init-prompt-flag-mismatch.md (committed as part of
    this batch since it shares the "exercising centos_server in Docker
    finally surfaced latent dotfiles install bugs" theme).
    
    The CentOS 7 sudo flavor still hits a separate Linuxbrew-vs-old-git
    issue (CentOS 7 ships git 1.8.x; Homebrew requires 2.7.0+); deferring
    that as a bootstrap-script change of larger scope. centos7-noroot
    (the realistic corporate scenario per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md) is
    unaffected by the Linuxbrew gate.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
